# Three things I got wrong about calibration

I spent a year telling people to calibrate their scanner before trusting it. I still believe that. But three of the reasons I gave were wrong, and it is worth saying which.

## I said thresholds were guesses

They are, when they ship. What I missed is that a guess with a label is more useful than a measurement without one. The shipped thresholds print an UNCALIBRATED banner on every run, and that banner did more to get people calibrating than any argument I made.

## I said five samples were enough

Five samples get you bands. They do not get you bands you should trust, and I let people think the two were the same. Below ten the tool now says "thin", and it should have said so from the start.

## I said calibration was a one-time job

It is not. A corpus grows, a register shifts, and the bands move underneath you. The fix is a lock: a named snapshot you calibrate against on purpose, not whatever the folder happens to contain today.

## What I would say now

Calibrate, yes. But read the banner, distrust thin bands, and lock what you like before it drifts. The tool was right; my reasons were the weak part.
